findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: pooled UC vs control log2FC is up in all eight cohorts [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.838]. In the same patients inflamed mucosa is higher than non-inflamed [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], and non-inflamed vs control is only a small rise [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. The change holds after adjusting for colon segment, age and sex [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.552]. CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk rise most likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a tissue-intrinsic change (cell-context specialist to confirm); it is a marker of local inflammation, and CXCR2 antagonists are in clinical development.

CXCL8 (IL-8) is strongly and consistently up across all eight cohorts [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687], and is higher in inflamed than paired non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.968]. Together with CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL1 and CXCL5 it defines a neutrophil-recruitment axis; part of the bulk signal comes from infiltrating immune cells.

IDO1 rises in all eight cohorts [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.102]. It is also modestly raised in non-inflamed UC mucosa [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.535], so it is mainly an inflammation-driven interferon-response gene, with some disease-level signal. It has no genetic support in the ranking, and immune-cell contribution is likely.

CHI3L1 has one of the largest and most reproducible increases, up in all eight cohorts [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913]. At protein level in independent inflamed UC mucosa the change is in the same direction but much smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607], and the proteomics authors did not call it significant. This supports a biomarker role, with a weaker protein-level effect than RNA.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis/metabolism gene, is lost in UC in all eight cohorts [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.039]. The loss is local to inflamed mucosa: non-inflamed mucosa is not different from control [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]. It replicates at protein level [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]. It is a strong marker of local inflammation, not a target.

S100A8 (calprotectin subunit) is up in all eight cohorts [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.793] and also rises at protein level in inflamed UC mucosa [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]. This is a neutrophil and myeloid product, so it reports immune infiltration and is a biomarker rather than a tissue-intrinsic target.

JAK2 has only a modest but highly reproducible rise, significant in all eight cohorts [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.8326]. Its convergence rank comes mainly from genetic association, literature and tractability rather than from expression size, so it is a genetics-supported target whose RNA change is small.

MMP3 is up in all eight cohorts [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.8223] and higher in inflamed than paired non-inflamed mucosa [gene=MMP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.337]. The MMP family (MMP1, MMP3, MMP7, MMP10) forms a stromal/epithelial tissue-remodelling signature that marks local inflammation; broad MMP inhibitors have a poor translational record.

AQP8 shows the strongest pooled decrease in the dataset, down in all eight cohorts [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633]. Together with CLDN8, SLC26A2, PCK1 and UGT2A3 it forms an epithelial absorptive/metabolic loss signature; these are biomarkers of epithelial damage, not targets.

DUOX2 (with DUOXA2) is a reproducible epithelial up-regulated gene, up in all eight cohorts [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033]. It reflects epithelial stress and antimicrobial response, and it has no genetic or drug support in the ranking.

caveats: Bulk biopsy changes in neutrophil/myeloid genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, IL1B, TREM1) may reflect infiltrating cells rather than a change inside tissue; the cell-context specialist should check with single-cell data and composition adjustment.
Heterogeneity between cohorts is high for most top genes (I2 around 0.9), so compare direction and significance, not size, across microarray and RNA-seq cohorts.
Protein-level checks were run only for CHI3L1, HMGCS2 and S100A8; not measured is not evidence against the other genes.
Adjusted-change check was run only for CXCR2 (MSCCR only).
Genes with few cohorts (SAA1, SAA2, DEFB4A/B) have fewer cohorts behind the pooled estimate and were not highlighted.
Convergence ranking mixes in literature and genetics; expression-only strength favours epithelial and inflammatory genes with no genetic support.
